label: batch-58
tail:
**Batch 58 authoring is complete.** The A page contains the perfect material postulate and two conditional theorems; the B page contains the uniform-background example. I added the published zero-derivative corollary needed to justify local circulation constancy, and expanded the example’s proof that the Minkowski connection coefficients vanish. The plan discrepancy and supplier status are recorded in the [batch notes](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/physics/research/physics-remaining-80-2026-10-17-batch-58.notes.md) and [dependency evidence](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/physics/research/physics-remaining-80-2026-10-17-batch-58.dependency-inputs.json).

I reviewed the relevant sections of [Gourgoulhon’s lecture](https://arxiv.org/pdf/gr-qc/0603009) and [Borghini’s lecture notes](https://www.physik.uni-bielefeld.de/~borghini/Teaching/Hydrodynamics15/Hydrodynamics.pdf). The source check passed for all four records, with no new stamps.

Scoped precheck, proof layout, rendercheck, depcheck, content policy and strict proof-contract validation all passed. The assigned dependency closure passed at levels 7, 7, 8 and 8. The full-run level check still reports unrelated incomplete inventories and stale levels elsewhere; this is documented without changes to those batches.

All four readiness decisions are **escalated** because supplier readiness remains unresolved: MC01 hashes are stale, the MC02 proofs inherit that hold, and the framework-units chain remains open through MI03/MI01. One readiness record needs owner attention: the example received a final proof clarification after its escalation was recorded, leaving its stored hash stale. The decision tool rejected refreshing it with “Only the owner may resolve this record.” I preserved the escalation and did not use `--owner`; an owner-controlled refresh is required before that record is current.
